info.about: GrimGrimoire is a 2007 real-time strategy video game developed by Vanillaware and published by Nippon Ichi Software and Koei (Europe) for the PlayStation 2. A remaster, GrimGrimoire OnceMore was released in Japan on PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch in 2022 and worldwide, along with a PlayStation 5 version, in 2023.
info.trivia: Vanillaware's real-time strategy game, remastered as OnceMore in 2023.
info.why: A small print run for a niche genre on PS2, and the remaster renewed attention.

info.about: Disgaea: Hour of Darkness is a tactical role-playing video game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Damage numbers run into the millions and the level cap is 9999, which was the joke and the point.
info.why: The first Atlus pressing was small; the series only became reliably popular from the sequels onwards.

info.about: Disgaea 2: Cursed Memories is a tactical role-playing game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2 video game console. Disgaea 2 is the sequel to 2003's Disgaea: Hour of Darkness and was released for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: The sequel to Hour of Darkness, later ported to PSP and PC.
info.why: Moderate supply and several other versions keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Phantom Brave is a tactical role-playing game for the PlayStation 2 video game console, developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software. It was released on January 22, 2004 in Japan, on August 31, 2004 in North America and on February 4, 2005 in Europe.
info.trivia: Nippon Ichi's grid-free tactics game, ported to Wii, PSP and PC.
info.why: Moderate supply and many ports keep the PS2 disc mid-priced.

info.about: La Pucelle: Tactics is a tactical role-playing game developed by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2. It was released in Japan in January 2002, and in North America by Mastiff in May 2004.
info.trivia: Nippon Ichi's first tactics game, published in the West by Mastiff.
info.why: A small print run from a minor publisher and no re-release keep it scarce.

games.title: Makai Kingdom: Chronicles of the Sacred Tome

info.about: Makai Kingdom: Chronicles of the Sacred Tome is a tactical role-playing game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software. It was initially released for PlayStation 2 on March 17, 2005 in Japan, July 26 in North America, and October 28 in Europe.
info.trivia: A Nippon Ichi tactics game with free movement, remastered in 2021.
info.why: A moderate print run; the remaster covers players but not the disc.

info.about: Ar tonelico: Melody of Elemia, released in Japan as Ar tonelico: The Girl Who Keeps Singing at the End of the World is a role-playing video game developed by Gust Corporation for the PlayStation 2 and originally published by Banpresto in 2006.
info.trivia: A Gust RPG built around song magic, published by NIS America in 2007.
info.why: A small print run and no re-release; the series never left PlayStation.

games.title: Ar tonelico II: Melody of Metafalica

info.about: Ar tonelico II: Melody of Metafalica, known in Japan as Ar tonelico II: Sekai ni Hibiku Shōjo-tachi no Metafalica is a role-playing video game, developed by Gust for the PlayStation 2 which was released in Japan on October 25, 2007, in North America on January 20, 2009, and was set to be released in the EU on 29 May 2009, but a problem with the barcode delayed it by a week.
info.trivia: The North American release in 2009 shipped with a bug that could crash the final boss fight.
info.why: A very late, small print run for a niche RPG, and no re-release, make it one of the priciest NIS America PS2 titles.

info.about: Mana Khemia: Alchemists of Al-Revis is a role-playing video game developed by Gust Co. Ltd. in 2007 for the PlayStation 2. The game is the ninth entry to Gust's Atelier series and incorporates elements of standard turn-based combat and alchemy.
info.trivia: A Gust RPG set in an alchemy academy, later ported to PSP as Student Alliance.
info.why: A small print run and no re-release of this version keep it scarce.

info.about: Steambot Chronicles is a 2005 action role-playing game developed and published by Irem Software Engineering in Japan for the PlayStation 2, set during an alternate universe Industrial Revolution where machines called 'Trotmobiles' became the standard for modern transportation and industrial machinery.
info.trivia: Irem's open-ended adventure with mechs, harmonica busking and a band to join, published by Atlus in 2006.
info.why: A small Atlus print run for a cult title that was never re-released.

info.about: A two-disc set bringing Growlanser II and Growlanser III to North America in 2004, and the final release from Working Designs.
info.trivia: Working Designs' final release before the publisher closed in 2005, bundling Growlanser II and III with a deluxe edition.
info.why: A small print run from a publisher that no longer exists, with a collector following for everything Working Designs made.

info.about: Growlanser: Heritage of War is a tactical role-playing video game for the PlayStation 2. It was developed by Career Soft, and published in Japan by Atlus in 2006.
info.trivia: Atlus brought the fifth Growlanser to the US in 2007.
info.why: A small late-life print run and no re-release.

info.about: Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater is a 2004 action-adventure stealth game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. It was released in late 2004 in North America and Japan, and in early 2005 in Europe and Australia.
info.trivia: A three-disc re-release adding a movable camera, online play and the original MSX Metal Gear games.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than Snake Eater and preferred for its camera and the MSX games, so it prices well above the original.

games.title: Zone of the Enders: The 2nd Runner

info.about: Zone of the Enders: The 2nd Runner, known in Japan as Anubis: Zone of the Enders, is an action hack and slash video game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 in 2003. The sequel to Zone of the Enders is based around mecha combat with the player once again controlling the "Orbital Frame" Jehuty.
info.trivia: Kojima Productions' mech game with a hand-drawn art style, remastered twice since.
info.why: Moderate supply; the HD and Mars remasters give players other routes, so the disc is mid-priced.

info.about: Devil May Cry 3: Dante's Awakening is a 2005 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. The game is a prequel to the original Devil May Cry, featuring a younger Dante.
info.trivia: A revised release adding a playable Vergil and an easier difficulty for the West.
info.why: Sold as a Greatest Hits title in large numbers, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Resident Evil Outbreak is a survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It was released on December 11, 2003 in Japan, on March 30, 2004 in North America, and on September 17, 2004 in PAL regions.
info.trivia: The first online Resident Evil; the US servers closed in 2007.
info.why: Common enough, but with online play gone and no re-release, the disc is the only way to own it.

info.about: Resident Evil Outbreak: File #2 is a survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom with online playability for the PlayStation 2. It is the sequel to Resident Evil Outbreak, and the final installment of the spin-off series.
info.trivia: A second set of scenarios released in 2005, again with online play that has since closed.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the first Outbreak and never re-released, so it prices above it.

info.about: Gradius V is a 2004 scrolling shooter video game published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. It was largely developed under contract by Treasure, who had previously worked on Radiant Silvergun and Ikaruga.
info.trivia: Treasure developed this entry for Konami, with a soundtrack by Hitoshi Sakimoto.
info.why: A small print run for a shooter and no Western re-release keep it among the pricier PS2 shooters.

info.about: R-Type Final is a horizontal shooter video game by Irem for the PlayStation 2 video game console. It was planned to be the last mainline game in the R-Type series.
info.trivia: Irem's farewell to the series, with more than a hundred unlockable ships.
info.why: A modest print run for a shooter; the 2021 sequel renewed interest without replacing it.

info.about: Raiden III is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by MOSS and released in as an arcade video game in 2005. It is the fourth game in Seibu Kaihatsu's Raiden series; it is the first installment in the series to be developed by MOSS as it consists of former Seibu Kaihatsu employees who bought the rights to the series.
info.trivia: UFO Interactive brought the arcade shooter to the US in 2007.
info.why: A tiny late-life print run from a minor publisher makes it one of the scarcest PS2 shooters.

info.about: Castlevania: Lament of Innocence is a 2003 action-adventure game developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 console. Part of Konami's Castlevania video game series, it is the first installment of the series on the PlayStation 2 and the third to make use of a 3D style of gameplay.
info.trivia: The series' first 3D entry that was well received, set at the origin of the Belmont curse.
info.why: Moderate supply and no re-release keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Castlevania: Curse of Darkness is a 2005 action role-playing game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox. It is the fourth 3D title in the Castlevania series, following Castlevania: Lament of Innocence (2003).
info.trivia: A sequel to Castlevania III with a companion-raising system.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than Lament of Innocence and never re-released, so it prices above it.

info.about: Contra: Shattered Soldier is a video game that is part of the Contra series by Konami. It was developed by Team Kijirushi, a group of staff members within Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo.
info.trivia: Konami's return to 2D Contra after two panned PlayStation entries.
info.why: A modest print run for a hard, niche game and no re-release keep it climbing.

info.about: Marvel vs. Capcom 2: New Age of Heroes is a 2000 crossover fighting game developed and published by Capcom for arcades. It is the fourth installment in the Marvel vs. Capcom series, which features characters from both Capcom's video game franchises and comic book series published by Marvel Comics.
info.trivia: Capcom's Marvel licence lapsed, and the game vanished from stores for over a decade until the 2024 collection.
info.why: A generation of players who could not buy it anywhere kept demand for the disc high; the 2024 re-release eased it only slightly.

info.about: Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millennium 2001 is a 2001 crossover fighting game developed and published by Capcom. The sequel to Capcom vs. SNK: Millennium Fight 2000 (2000) and an entry in the SNK vs. Capcom series, it was originally released on NAOMI hardware in arcades, with Sega handling the North American arcade release.
info.trivia: The PS2 version added extra grooves and is the basis of the competitive scene's preferred build.
info.why: Moderate supply, but sustained tournament interest and a long gap without re-release keep it expensive.

info.about: Guilty Gear X2, also known as Guilty Gear XX and subtitled The Midnight Carnival in Japan, is a fighting game developed by Arc System Works and published by Sammy Studios. The third main installment of the Guilty Gear series, Guilty Gear X2 furthered the plot of the series, as well as introduced new characters and gameplay mechanics.
info.trivia: A revision released in 2007, later superseded by Plus and Plus R on other platforms.
info.why: A late, small print run of one specific revision, so it is scarcer than the game itself.

info.about: The Warriors is a 2005 beat 'em up video game developed by Rockstar Toronto and published by Rockstar Games. Based on the 1979 film of the same name; it was released in October 2005 for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox, and February 2007 for the PlayStation Portable; the PSP port was developed by Rockstar Leeds.
info.trivia: Rockstar's adaptation of the 1979 film, with the original cast returning to voice their characters.
info.why: A moderate print run; the licence makes re-release complicated, and a PS4 download came only in 2016.

info.about: Bully is a 2006 action-adventure video game developed by Rockstar Vancouver and published by Rockstar Games. Set in the fictional New England town of Bullworth, the game follows juvenile delinquent student Jimmy Hopkins, who is involuntarily enrolled at Bullworth Academy, the town's prestigious boarding school.
info.trivia: Rockstar Vancouver's school-set open world, briefly the subject of a lawsuit before release.
info.why: The game was reprinted as a Greatest Hits title, so original black-label copies carry the premium; the Scholarship Edition ports keep the game itself available.

info.about: Def Jam: Fight for NY is a 3D fighting video game developed by AKI Corporation and EA Canada and published by EA Games. It was released for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox on September 21, 2004.
info.trivia: A wrestling game whose roster is licensed rappers, from Method Man to Snoop Dogg.
info.why: Dozens of licensed artists and tracks make a re-release practically impossible, and a cult following keeps demand high.

info.about: Killer7 is a 2005 action-adventure game developed by Grasshopper Manufacture and Capcom and published by Capcom for the GameCube and PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Suda51's cel-shaded assassin game, one of the Capcom Five, ported to PS2 with censorship changes.
info.why: Moderate supply; a PC port in 2018 covers players, so prices are mid-range.

info.about: Gungrave is a 2002 Japanese third-person shooter video game developed and published by Red Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Red Entertainment's shooter with character designs by Yasuhiro Nightow of Trigun.
info.why: Moderate supply and no re-release; the 2022 sequel renewed some interest.

info.about: Gungrave: Overdose is a PlayStation 2 third-person shooter video game developed by animation studio Ikusabune and published by Red Entertainment in Japan and by Mastiff in North America, and a direct sequel to Gungrave. The game was released on March 4, 2004, in Japan, September 15, 2004, in North America and October 7, 2005, in the PAL regions.
info.trivia: A budget-priced sequel that sold for twenty dollars at launch.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the first game and never re-released, so it prices above it.

games.title: Blood Will Tell: Tezuka Osamu's Dororo

info.about: Blood Will Tell: Tezuka Osamu's Dororo, released as Dororo (どろろ) in Japan, is a 2004 PlayStation 2 game released by Sega. It is based on the Japanese manga series Dororo, which was created by Osamu Tezuka.
info.trivia: Sega's adaptation of Osamu Tezuka's manga Dororo, in which the hero reclaims his stolen body parts.
info.why: A small US print run for an oddity that was never re-released, so it is one of the scarcer Sega PS2 titles.

info.about: Chulip (チュウリップ), stylized as Chu♥lip, is an adventure/simulation video game developed by Punchline and released on October 3, 2002, in Japan by Victor Interactive Software for the PlayStation 2. After numerous delays, the game was released in North America by Natsume Inc. on February 13, 2007, as a GameStop-exclusive title.
info.trivia: A game about kissing everyone in town, published in the US by Natsume in 2007.
info.why: A tiny late-life print run for a cult title; among the rarest US PS2 discs.

info.about: Way of the Samurai 2 is a PlayStation 2 (PS2) action-adventure game released in 2003.
info.trivia: Acquire's open-ended samurai sandbox, published in the US by Capcom.
info.why: A modest print run and no re-release keep it above average.

info.about: Front Mission 4, also known in Japan as Front Mission Fourth, is a tactical role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2. It is the fourth main installment of the Front Mission series.
info.trivia: The only PS2 Front Mission released in the West.
info.why: Moderate supply and no remake, unlike earlier entries, keep it steady.

info.about: Ring of Red is an alternate history turn-based strategy video game released by Konami for the PlayStation 2 console. It was one of the first PlayStation 2 games made with CD-ROM-based technology.
info.trivia: Konami's alternate-history mech tactics game, an early PS2 release.
info.why: A small print run for a niche strategy game and no re-release.

info.about: Klonoa 2: Lunatea's Veil is a 2001 platform game developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. It is the third installment in the Klonoa series and a sequel to Klonoa: Moonlight Museum (1999).
info.trivia: Namco's 2.5D platformer, unreissued until the 2022 Phantasy Reverie collection.
info.why: A modest print run and twenty years without a re-release keep the disc pricey even after the collection.

info.about: TimeSplitters: Future Perfect is a 2005 first-person shooter video game developed by Free Radical Design and published by Electronic Arts for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox.
info.trivia: Free Radical's third and last TimeSplitters, with a map maker and time-travelling co-op.
info.why: The studio's collapse means no re-release, and it is the series' most requested entry.

info.about: Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King is a 2004 role-playing video game developed by Level-5 and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2. It was first released in Japan in November 2004, followed by North America in November 2005 and PAL regions in April 2006.
info.trivia: The first-run black-label release, which shipped with a Final Fantasy XII demo disc.
info.why: The game is common, so the premium is for the black label with the demo disc over the Greatest Hits reprint.

info.about: Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII is a 2007 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: The combat runs on a slot machine that fires abilities and cutscenes at random while you fight.
info.why: The original UMD predates the Reunion remaster, and sealed copies are chased by Final Fantasy VII collectors.

info.about: Persona 3, released outside Japan as Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 3, is a 2006 role-playing video game developed by Atlus. It is the fourth main installment in the Persona series, which is part of the larger Megami Tensei franchise.
info.trivia: It added a female protagonist and remains the only version with that route until the 2023 remaster.
info.why: Popular and reprinted, so the UMD is affordable; the remaster gives most players a digital route.

info.about: Persona 2: Innocent Sin is a 1999 role-playing video game developed and published by Atlus for the PlayStation. It is the second entry in the Persona series, itself a subseries of the Megami Tensei franchise, and acts as a sequel to the original Persona.
info.trivia: The first time Innocent Sin was released outside Japan, in September 2011 near the end of the PSP's life.
info.why: Atlus printed very few copies that late, and it has never been re-released, so it is one of the most expensive PSP games.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together

info.about: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together is a 1995 tactical role-playing game developed and published by Quest Corporation for the Super Famicom. It was later ported to the Sega Saturn (1996) and the PlayStation (1997), the latter released in North America in 1998 by Atlus USA.
info.trivia: A full remake by the original team with a rewritten script; Reborn revised it again in 2022.
info.why: Moderate supply and the Reborn release keep the UMD mid-priced.

games.title: Final Fantasy Tactics: The War of the Lions

info.about: Final Fantasy Tactics: The War of the Lions is a 2007 tactical role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation Portable (PSP).
info.trivia: A retranslation of the PlayStation classic with new cutscenes and characters.
info.why: Sold well and was ported to phones, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Valkyria Chronicles II is a tactical role-playing video game developed and published by Sega for the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: The only Valkyria Chronicles game never re-released on any other platform.
info.why: A modest print run and no remaster, unlike the first and fourth games, make it the expensive one of the series.

info.about: Jeanne d'Arc is a tactical role-playing video game developed by Level-5 and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. The game was released in Japan on November 22, 2006 and North America on August 21, 2007.
info.trivia: Level-5 recast the Hundred Years War as a fantasy campaign with demons behind the English crown.
info.why: A small print run for a strategy game on a handheld that was not selling strategy games, and no reissue since.

info.about: Ys Seven is a 2009 action role-playing game developed and published in Japan by Nihon Falcom.
info.trivia: XSEED's premium edition shipped with a soundtrack CD and art book.
info.why: A small XSEED print run; the 2017 PC port covers players but not collectors.

info.about: Ys: The Oath in Felghana is a 2005 action role-playing game developed by Nihon Falcom.
info.trivia: A remake of Ys III with a soundtrack widely considered Falcom's best.
info.why: A small print run, and the only physical Western release of the game.

info.about: Ys I & II is a 1989 action role-playing game developed by Alfa System and published by Hudson Soft for the PC Engine CD-ROM².
info.trivia: The first two Ys games in one remake, with three selectable soundtracks.
info.why: A small XSEED pressing that was never repeated on a console.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky

info.about: The Legend of Heroes: Trails in the Sky, also known as Trails in the Sky FC, is a 2004 role-playing video game developed by Nihon Falcom. The game is the first in the Trails series, itself a part of the larger The Legend of Heroes series.
info.trivia: The series' first Western release, in 2011; a full remake followed in 2025.
info.why: XSEED printed few copies of a very long RPG for a shrinking system, and the 2025 remake drove new interest in where the series began.

info.about: Gurumin: A Monstrous Adventure is a 2004 action role-playing game developed by Nihon Falcom. The game stars a girl named Parin who wields a drill weapon who fights against phantoms who attack a village of monsters.
info.trivia: Falcom made it for children and then filled it with the same combat depth as its adult-facing series.
info.why: Mastiff was a small publisher and the UMD run was tiny.

info.about: Half-Minute Hero is a hybrid real-time strategy action role-playing shoot 'em up video game developed by Opus. It was initially released as a PlayStation Portable exclusive in Japan on May 28, 2009, later in North America on October 13, and in Europe on February 19, 2010.
info.trivia: An RPG played in thirty-second bursts, published by XSEED in 2009.
info.why: A small print run; the PC and Xbox versions are digital, so the UMD is the only physical copy.

info.about: Castlevania: The Dracula X Chronicles is a 2007 platform game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation Portable. The game is a remake of Castlevania: Rondo of Blood (1993) with 2.5D graphics, and marks the first time that Rondo of Blood was released outside of Japan.
info.trivia: It includes the previously Japan-only Rondo of Blood and a hidden copy of Symphony of the Night.
info.why: Two classics on one disc kept demand high until the 2018 Requiem release, and the UMD remains the only portable version.

info.about: Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker is a 2010 stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami. It is the seventh Metal Gear game written, directed, and designed by Hideo Kojima, and the fifth installment of the Metal Gear Solid series, as well as the fourth Metal Gear game made specifically for the PlayStation Portable, following Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops.
info.trivia: Kojima's full-scale Metal Gear built for a handheld, later included in the HD Collection.
info.why: Common, and available in HD elsewhere, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Metal Gear Solid: Portable Ops, officially abbreviated MPO, is a 2006 action-adventure stealth game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: Kojima Productions' first PSP Metal Gear, later sidelined from the series canon and never re-released.
info.why: The only way to play it is the UMD, which keeps demand steady despite a large print run.

info.about: Monster Hunter Freedom Unite is an action role-playing game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation Portable and iOS.
info.trivia: The game that made Monster Hunter a phenomenon in Japan, with hundreds of hours of content.
info.why: Sold in large numbers, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Patapon 3 is a 2011 rhythm video game developed by Pyramid and Japan Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. It is the final installment in the Patapon series and a sequel to Patapon 2 (2008).
info.trivia: The third game arrived in 2011 and, unlike its predecessors, never received a PS4 remaster.
info.why: A late, small print run and no re-release make it the expensive Patapon.

info.about: Patapon 2 is a 2008 rhythm video game developed by Pyramid and Japan Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. It is a direct sequel to Patapon, and like its predecessor, uses the same unique genre that combines rhythm and strategy.
info.trivia: In North America it was sold as a box containing a download voucher rather than a UMD.
info.why: No US disc exists, so physical copies are European or Japanese imports, and the 2020 remaster did not change that.

info.about: LocoRoco is a 2006 platform video game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. The game was conceived by Tsutomu Kouno, who strived to create a game that was different from other titles being released for the PSP at the time.
info.trivia: Sony Japan Studio's tilt-the-world platformer, remastered for PS4 in 2017.
info.why: Sony sold it in large numbers and remastered it for PS4 in 2017, so supply is deep and the UMD stays cheap.

info.about: Lumines: Puzzle Fusion is a 2004 puzzle video game developed by Q Entertainment and published for the PlayStation Portable by Bandai in Japan and by Ubisoft elsewhere. The gameplay tasks players to arrange descending two-colored 2×2 blocks to create 2×2 squares of matching color.
info.trivia: A launch title from Tetsuya Mizuguchi that became the system's defining puzzle game.
info.why: Very common and re-released many times, so the UMD is cheap.

games.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus

info.about: God of War: Chains of Olympus is a 2008 action-adventure game developed by Ready at Dawn, and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). It was first released for the PlayStation Portable (PSP) handheld console on March 4, 2008.
info.trivia: Ready at Dawn's prequel was the handheld's technical showpiece.
info.why: Common, and included in an HD collection on PS3, so prices are low.

games.title: God of War: Ghost of Sparta

info.about: God of War: Ghost of Sparta is a 2010 action-adventure game developed by Ready at Dawn and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). It was first released for the PlayStation Portable (PSP) handheld console on November 2, 2010.
info.trivia: Released in late 2010, after most PSP owners had moved on.
info.why: A smaller late-life print run than Chains of Olympus makes it the pricier of the pair.

info.about: Daxter is a 2006 platform video game developed by Ready at Dawn and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: Ready at Dawn's debut, often bundled with the console.
info.why: It was bundled with the console for years, so copies are everywhere and prices stay low regardless of condition.

info.about: Syphon Filter: Dark Mirror is a 2006 third-person shooter video game developed by Bend Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable and PlayStation 2. It is the fifth installment in the Syphon Filter franchise and a sequel to 2004's Syphon Filter: The Omega Strain.
info.trivia: Sony Bend's revival of the series, later ported to PS2.
info.why: A large first-party print run and a later PS2 port keep supply deep, so prices are driven by condition rather than scarcity.

info.about: Wipeout Pure is a 2005 racing video game developed by Studio Liverpool and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. It was released as a launch title for the platform in North America and PAL territories, in March and September respectively.
info.trivia: A launch title that received free downloadable tracks, unusual for 2005.
info.why: A launch title sold in very large numbers, so supply is deep and prices stay low; complete copies are easy to find.

info.about: Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep is a 2010 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix in collaboration with Disney Interactive Studios for the PlayStation Portable, serving as the sixth installment in the Kingdom Hearts series. The game was released on UMD worldwide in 2010.
info.trivia: A prequel with three protagonists, later remastered in the PS3 collection.
info.why: Common, and the remaster covers most players, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Dissidia 012 Final Fantasy is a 2011 fighting game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation Portable as part of the Final Fantasy series. It was developed by the company's 1st Production Department and released worldwide in March 2011.
info.trivia: A prequel-expansion that includes the whole first Dissidia inside it.
info.why: Released in 2011 as the system wound down, so supply is thinner than the first game.

info.about: Class of Heroes is a role-playing video game dungeon crawler for the PlayStation Portable developed by Zero Div and published by Acquire in Japan and Atlus in North America. In Japan, the game was released on August 26, 2008; in North America, the game was released on June 9, 2009, by Atlus.
info.trivia: A first-person dungeon crawler in the Wizardry tradition, released when almost nobody was making them for handhelds.
info.why: Notoriously low print run, and the sequel's troubled release made the first game harder to find still.

info.about: Riviera: The Promised Land is a 2002 role-playing video game developed by Sting Entertainment. It was originally released for WonderSwan Color as the first episode of the Dept.
info.trivia: Sting's RPG began on WonderSwan and Game Boy Advance; the PSP version added voice acting.
info.why: A small Atlus print run for a niche remake that was never re-released.

info.about: Knights in the Nightmare is a role-playing video game developed by Sting Entertainment. It is the fourth episode in the Dept.
info.trivia: A Sting RPG played with a cursor, originally on DS, ported with a bonus copy of Yggdra Union.
info.why: A small Atlus print run in 2010, and no digital re-release, keep it scarce.

info.about: Yggdra Union: We'll Never Fight Alone is a tactical role-playing game for the Game Boy Advance and PlayStation Portable, developed by Sting Entertainment as the second episode of the Dept. Heaven saga of games.
info.trivia: A card-driven tactics game from Sting, remade from the Game Boy Advance original.
info.why: A small Atlus print run and no re-release.

info.about: Corpse Party, released in Japan as Corpse Party: BloodCovered, is a horror adventure game developed by Team GrisGris and published by Xseed Games for Microsoft Windows. Originally developed as Corpse Party: NewChapter for Japanese mobile phones, it is a remake of the 1996 NEC PC-9801 video game Corpse-Party, and the second game in the Corpse Party series.
info.trivia: It began as a 1996 amateur PC-98 game and was remade fifteen years later for a console audience.
info.why: The physical UMD was a limited run in a mostly digital release window.

info.about: Silent Hill: Shattered Memories is a 2009 survival horror game developed by Climax Studios and published by Konami. It was released in December for the Wii and ported to the PlayStation 2 and PlayStation Portable platforms in January 2010.
info.trivia: A re-imagining of the first game built around a psychological profile of the player.
info.why: The Wii version is common; the PSP and PS2 versions were printed in far smaller numbers, so this one prices well above it.

info.about: Silent Hill: Origins is a 2007 survival horror game developed by Climax Studios and published by Konami. It was released worldwide in late 2007 for the PlayStation Portable, beginning in early November with the United Kingdom.
info.trivia: The first Silent Hill made outside Japan, a prequel by Climax Studios.
info.why: A moderate print run and a PS2 port keep it mid-priced.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories

info.about: Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a 2006 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar Leeds and Rockstar North, and published by Rockstar Games. The tenth entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, the game was initially released as a PlayStation Portable exclusive in October 2006.
info.trivia: The last Grand Theft Auto built for a handheld until the phone ports.
info.why: Rockstar sold millions on PSP and ported it to PS2, so supply is deep and prices stay low regardless of condition.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

info.about: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories is a 2005 action-adventure game developed in a collaboration between Rockstar Leeds and Rockstar North, and published by Rockstar Games. The ninth installment in the Grand Theft Auto series, it was initially released as a PlayStation Portable exclusive in October 2005.
info.trivia: The PSP's biggest seller in its first year.
info.why: The best-selling PSP game of its first year, later ported to PS2 and phones, so copies are everywhere and prices stay low.

games.title: Prinny: Can I Really Be the Hero?

info.about: Prinny: Can I Really Be the Hero? is a 2D side-scrolling comedy platform video game for the PlayStation Portable, developed by Nippon Ichi Software.
info.trivia: A brutally hard platformer starring Disgaea's penguin servants, with a thousand lives to burn.
info.why: A moderate NIS America print run; the 2020 Switch collection covers players but not the UMD.

info.about: Disgaea: Hour of Darkness is a tactical role-playing video game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: A port of the PS2 original with a new campaign for Etna.
info.why: Common and re-released digitally, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Star Ocean is a 1996 action role-playing game developed by tri-Ace and published by Enix for the Super Famicom. The first game in the Star Ocean series, it was released only in Japan in July 1996, and was the first game developed by tri-Ace, consisting of staff that had previously left Wolf Team due to being unhappy with the development process for Tales of Phantasia with Namco in 1995.
info.trivia: The first Western release of the original Star Ocean, remade in the Second Story engine.
info.why: Moderate supply, and a 2019 remaster gives players another route, so prices are mid-range.

info.about: Brave Story: New Traveler is a role-playing video game developed by Game Republic and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. It is based on the manga adaptation of Brave Story.
info.trivia: An RPG based on Miyuki Miyabe's novel, published in the West by XSEED in 2007.
info.why: One of XSEED's earliest releases, printed in small numbers and never re-released.

info.about: Undead Knights is an action-adventure video game developed by Team Tachyon and Now Production and published by Tecmo for the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: Tecmo's action game about turning enemies into a zombie army, released in 2009.
info.why: A small print run for a cult title that was never re-released.

info.about: Persona 4, released outside Japan as Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 4, is a 2008 role-playing video game by Atlus. It is chronologically the fifth installment in the Persona series, itself a part of the larger Megami Tensei franchise, and was released for the PlayStation 2 in Japan in July 2008, North America in December 2008, and in Europe and Australia in March 2009.
info.trivia: The Vita's defining game, and the reason a lot of people bought the handheld at all.
info.why: The PS Vita store closure made physical carts the only lasting way to own Vita games, and this is the one everybody wants.

annotation.note: The PS Vita store closure announcement made physical carts the only lasting way to own Vita games.

info.about: Ys: Memories of Celceta is a 2012 action role-playing game developed by Nihon Falcom. An installment in the Ys series, it was originally released for the PlayStation Vita in Japan in September 2012.
info.trivia: The fourth Ys story, retold by Falcom itself after two earlier versions were made by other studios.
info.why: A modest physical run from a small publisher, on a handheld with a closed storefront.

info.about: Muramasa: The Demon Blade is a 2009 action role-playing game developed by Vanillaware and published for the Wii by Marvelous Entertainment (Japan), Ignition Entertainment, and Rising Star Games (Europe).
info.trivia: Vanillaware redrew the Wii original at the Vita's higher resolution rather than upscaling it.
info.why: A small physical run for a hand-drawn game on a console whose store has since closed.

info.about: Dragon's Crown is a 2013 action role-playing game developed by Vanillaware for the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita. The game was published in Japan and North America by Atlus and in PAL regions by NIS America.
info.trivia: Every backdrop is a hand-painted plate; the game was in development for years before Atlus picked it up.
info.why: Physical Vita copies are scarce and the store closure removed the digital alternative.

info.about: Odin Sphere is an action role-playing game developed by Vanillaware for the PlayStation 2. It was published by Atlus in 2007, and by Square Enix in 2008.
info.trivia: Vanillaware's remake of the PS2 game, redrawn for HD with a reworked battle system.
info.why: The Vita version was the smallest run of the three platforms, and Vita physical releases dried up soon after.

info.about: Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc is a visual novel adventure game developed and published by Spike. The first installment in the Danganronpa series, it was originally released for the PlayStation Portable in Japan in November 2010.
info.trivia: The series' first Western release, in 2014, with a limited edition from NIS America.
info.why: Ported to most platforms since, so the game is easy to find; the Vita disc trades on being the original Western version.

info.about: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair is a 2012 visual novel developed by Spike Chunsoft. It is the second game in the Danganronpa franchise following Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc (2010).
info.trivia: The trials are argued in real time, and you shoot down testimony with literal ammunition.
info.why: Vita physical copies are increasingly hard to find complete, and the series has a devoted following.

games.title: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls

info.about: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls is an action-adventure and third-person shooter video game developed by Spike Chunsoft. It is a spin-off in the Danganronpa series, set in between the events of Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc and Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair.
info.trivia: A third-person shooter spin-off rather than a visual novel, released in 2015.
info.why: A smaller print run than the main games and a smaller audience for the spin-off keep it above them.

info.about: Zero Escape: Virtue's Last Reward is a 2012 adventure game developed by Chunsoft. It is the second installment in the Zero Escape series, and was originally released for the Nintendo 3DS and PlayStation Vita.
info.trivia: Aksys published it in 2012 in a run small enough that the Vita version sold out quickly.
info.why: A small Aksys print run; the 2017 Nonary Games collection covers players but not this version.

info.about: Steins;Gate is a 2009 science fiction visual novel game developed by 5pb. and Nitroplus. It is the second game in the Science Adventure series, following Chaos;Head.
info.trivia: The visual novel's first Western console release, published by PQube in 2015.
info.why: A small print run for a text-heavy game, and the Vita version was never reprinted.

info.about: Corpse Party: Blood Drive is a 2014 video game developed by Team GrisGris and 5pb. and published by 5pb. It was localized by XSEED and published for the PlayStation Vita in late 2015, digitally and physically.
info.trivia: XSEED published the finale of the story in 2015 with an Everafter Edition.
info.why: A small print run for a niche horror series, and no re-release of the Vita version.

info.about: Gravity Rush, known in Japan as Gravity Daze, is a 2012 action-adventure video game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita. Gravity Rush Remastered, a high definition remaster developed by Bluepoint Games for the PlayStation 4, was released in 2015 in Japan and 2016 in the West.
info.trivia: You do not jump, you fall in a direction of your choosing, which took the art team a French comics look to sell.
info.why: A launch-window Vita exclusive whose physical run predates the remaster, on a system with a closed store.

info.about: Tearaway is a platform adventure video game developed by Media Molecule and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita. The game was announced at Gamescom on 15 August 2012 and released on 20 November 2013 in Australia, on 22 November in Europe, North America and India, and 5 December 2013 in Japan.
info.trivia: Media Molecule's papercraft platformer, built around the Vita's rear touch pad.
info.why: A first-party release printed in good numbers; the PS4 Unfolded version is a remake, so this is the only version with the touch controls.

info.about: Soul Sacrifice is a 2013 action role-playing video game developed by Marvelous AQL and Japan Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita.
info.trivia: In North America the expanded Delta version was sold only as a download.
info.why: No US disc exists, so physical copies are European or Japanese imports.

info.about: Freedom Wars is a 2014 action role-playing video game developed by Dimps and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita. Set in the distant future where the majority of humankind is imprisoned in penal city-states known as Panopticons which wage war against one another, the game involves players cooperating to fight enemies and contribute towards their Panopticon.
info.trivia: You begin the game serving a one-million-year prison sentence and reduce it by doing missions.
info.why: A late first-party Vita release with a limited physical run.

info.about: Killzone: Mercenary is a 2013 first-person shooter video game developed by Guerrilla Cambridge and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita.
info.trivia: Guerrilla Cambridge's shooter was the handheld's technical showpiece.
info.why: A first-party release in good supply, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Uncharted: Golden Abyss is a 2011 action-adventure game developed by Bend Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita. A spin-off of Naughty Dog's Uncharted series, the game was released as a launch title for the console.
info.trivia: A launch title from Sony Bend, and the only Uncharted never ported to another platform.
info.why: Common as a launch title, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Wipeout 2048 is a 2012 racing video game developed by Studio Liverpool and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita. The ninth instalment of the Wipeout series, it was a launch game for the console.
info.trivia: The last game from Studio Liverpool before Sony closed it in 2012.
info.why: A launch title, so supply is fine; the studio's closure and the Omega Collection port keep interest steady.

info.about: Severed is an action-adventure video game developed and published by DrinkBox Studios for the PlayStation Vita, iOS, Wii U, Nintendo 3DS and Nintendo Switch. It was released on April 26, 2016, in North America and Europe for the PlayStation Vita and it was released on Wii U and iOS on September 22, 2016.

Salt and Sanctuary is a 2D action role-playing video game developed and published by Ska Studios. The game was released on March 15, 2016 for the PlayStation 4, with later releases for Microsoft Windows, macOS, Linux, PlayStation Vita, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch.

Spelunky is a 2008 platform video game created by independent developer Derek Yu and released as source-available freeware for Microsoft Windows. It was remade for the Xbox 360 in 2012, with ports of the new version following for various platforms, including back to Microsoft Windows.

Rogue Legacy is a 2013 platform game with roguelike elements developed and published by Cellar Door Games. The game was released for Microsoft Windows, Linux, OS X, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, PlayStation Vita, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, and iOS.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel

info.about: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel is a 2013 role-playing video game developed by Nihon Falcom. The game is the sixth installment of the Trails series, itself a part of the larger The Legend of Heroes series, and follows Trails to Azure (2011).
info.trivia: XSEED's 2015 release came with a limited edition and a fifty-hour campaign.
info.why: A small print run for a long RPG; the PS4 and PC versions cover players, so the Vita disc is the collector's version.

games.title: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II

info.about: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II is a 2014 role-playing video game developed by Nihon Falcom.
info.trivia: The second half of the story, released in 2016 as Vita output was ending.
info.why: A smaller print run than the first game makes it the more expensive of the pair.

info.about: Toukiden: The Age of Demons is an action role-playing game developed by Omega Force for the PlayStation Portable and PlayStation Vita. It was released on June 27, 2013 in Japan.
info.trivia: An expanded version of Toukiden with new missions and demons.
info.why: A moderate print run; the PS4 version is more common, so the Vita disc prices above it.

games.title: Atelier Ayesha Plus: The Alchemist of Dusk

info.about: Atelier Ayesha: The Alchemist of Dusk is a Japanese role-playing video game developed by Gust Co. Ltd. The character designs are by Hidari. It is the fourteenth title in the Atelier series, coming after Atelier Meruru, but has a storyline independent from previous titles in the series.
info.trivia: The Vita version was sold in North America only as a download.
info.why: No US disc exists, so physical copies are European imports.

info.about: Atelier Escha & Logy: Alchemists of the Dusk Sky is a Japanese role-playing video game developed by Gust Co. Ltd. Given the project code "A15", it is the 15th game in the official Atelier series and the second installment of the Dusk storyline. Hidari remains as the character designer and the game runs on the LTGL engine.
info.trivia: The Vita version was sold in North America only as a download.
info.why: No US disc exists, so physical copies are European imports.

info.about: Digimon Story: Cyber Sleuth is a role-playing video game developed by Media.Vision and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment that was released in Japan on March 12, 2015 for PlayStation Vita and PlayStation 4. Part of the Digimon franchise, the game is the fifth installment in the Digimon Story series, following 2011's Super Xros Wars, and the first to be released on home consoles.
info.trivia: The Vita version was sold in North America only as a download; the PS4 disc was the physical release.
info.why: No US Vita disc exists, so physical copies are European or Asian imports.

info.about: Demon Gaze is a dungeon crawl video game developed by Kadokawa Games and Experience Inc. for the PlayStation Vita. Released in Japan on January 24, 2013, it was published in North America and Europe by NIS America in April 2014.
info.trivia: A dungeon crawler from Experience Inc., published by NIS America with a limited edition.
info.why: A small print run for a niche genre, and no re-release.

info.about: Operation Abyss: New Tokyo Legacy is a dungeon crawler-role playing video game, developed in 2014 by Experience Inc. and published by MAGES and 5pb.Games in Japan and NIS America internationally.
info.trivia: Another Experience Inc. dungeon crawler, published by NIS America in 2015.
info.why: A small print run and a niche audience keep it scarce.

info.about: Akiba's Trip: Undead & Undressed, released as Akiba's Trip 2 in Japan, is a 2013 action-adventure open-world video game for the PlayStation Vita, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, and Microsoft Windows by Acquire. It is the sequel to Akiba's Trip on the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: XSEED's 2014 release of the Akihabara brawler, later ported to PS4 and PC.
info.why: A moderate print run; the ports cover players, so the Vita disc is mid-priced.

info.about: Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus is a 2013 action video game developed by Tamsoft, and the second main title in the Senran Kagura series as the sequel to Senran Kagura Burst. The game revolves around four female ninja groups from dueling shinobi schools.
info.trivia: XSEED's 2014 release shipped a limited edition with a soundtrack and a shinobi-themed bra.
info.why: A modest print run; the PC port covers players, so the disc trades on being the first Western entry.

info.about: Senran Kagura: Estival Versus is a hack and slash video game developed by Tamsoft and published by Xseed Games, released for PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita in March 2016, and on PC on March 17, 2017. It is part of the Senran Kagura series and a sequel to Senran Kagura Shinovi Versus.
info.trivia: Released in 2016 with an Endless Summer limited edition; the PS4 version sold better.
info.why: The Vita version was the smaller run, so it prices above the PS4 disc.

info.about: God Eater 2 is a video game developed by Shift and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment on November 14, 2013, in Japan for PlayStation Vita and PlayStation Portable. It is a sequel to God Eater.
info.trivia: The Vita version was sold in North America only as a download; the PS4 disc was the physical release.
info.why: No US Vita disc exists, so physical copies are European or Asian imports.

info.about: Sword Art Online: Hollow Realization is a Japanese video game developed by Aquria and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment for the PlayStation 4, PlayStation Vita, and Windows PC, based on the Japanese light novel series, Sword Art Online. It is the fourth video game in the series and the successor to Sword Art Online: Lost Song.
info.trivia: The Vita version was sold in North America only as a download; the PS4 disc was the physical release.
info.why: No US Vita disc exists, so physical copies are European or Asian imports.

info.about: Jak and Daxter Collection is a 2012 video game compilation developed by Mass Media and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. It is a collection of remastered ports of the first three games in Naughty Dog's Jak and Daxter series.
info.trivia: Mass Media ported Naughty Dog's PS2 trilogy to the handheld in 2013.
info.why: A modest print run for a late port on a small install base keeps it above typical Vita prices.

info.about: The three PlayStation 2 Sly Cooper games remastered in high definition, brought to PlayStation Vita in 2014.
info.trivia: The PS2 trilogy in HD, ported to Vita in 2014.
info.why: A modest print run on a small install base, and the only portable version of the games.

info.about: LittleBigPlanet PS Vita is a 2012 puzzle-platform video game developed by Tarsier Studios and Double Eleven and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Vita. It is the fourth main instalment of the LittleBigPlanet series.
info.trivia: Its servers closed in 2021, taking most of the user-made levels with it.
info.why: A first-party release in good supply, so prices are moderate.
